newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends sharply down on weather, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends sharply down on weather, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed sharply lower on crop weather and on a collapse in soybeans, traders said.

"Wheat and corn followed beans, and prospects of rain coming into the Western Plains also drove wheat down," said Joel Karlin, vice president of commodities for Chicago-based brokerage house Everen Securities.
Traders said there were prospects for an improvement in the ratings for the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop.
Meteorologists early Tuesday said there was a possibility of rain over the next five days in western Kansas.
Dry weather in western Kansas and portions of Nebraska has been holding back prospects for excellent wheat yields in those hard red winter wheat producing regions.
Traders said the weak expiration of the May contract also generated additional bearishness. The May expired at 1201 CDT Tuesday and was 11 cents per bushel lower at $3.81 per bushel.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed four to 14-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 14-1/4 at $3.80-1/2.
Also USDA's weekly crop briefs Monday, while showing a slight decline in U.S. winter wheat condition ratings, showed an improvement in the soft red winter wheat crop.
In Ohio, wheat ratings improved slightly.

In Illinois, wheat was rated 74 percent good to excellent which was unchanged from the previous week. In Indiana, wheat was 69 percent good to excellent, above the 62 a week earlier. Missouri wheat was mostly unchanged from the previous week.
In spread trading, LFG Futures did 1.5 million bushels of July/December at 18-1/2 to 18-3/4 cents, premium December, traders said.

In outright trading, Merrill Lynch Futures sold 3.5 million bushels of July, Dean Witter and Term Commodities each sold two million bushels of July and Lehman Brothers sold 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, above the 16,218 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 300 July $3.90 calls at 13-1/2 to 14-1/2 cents and bought 200 July $4.10 calls at six to 6-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, below the 6,905 traded Monday.
